historical_references.reference: Dhrishtaketu was a great king of Haihayas, ruled around 1300 BCE in the northern Indian subcontinent. He is best known for his intellectual prowess and philosophical discussions with the sage Bharadvaja.

Dhrishtadeva was a king of the Sisunaga Dynasty in Magadha, ruled around 5th Century BCE. He is mentioned in Buddhist texts for his generosity towards Buddhism and providing Ashoka with the royal patronage necessary for the Buddhist missionary activities to thrive.
